newsitem.title: UK: UK new car registrations down 7.8 pct in July - SMMT.
newsitem.headline: UK new car registrations down 7.8 pct in July - SMMT.

text.p: UK new car registrations fell 7.8 percent to 36,069 in July from 39,150 in the same month last year, the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders said on Wednesday.
New car registrations in the first seven months of the year were up 4.9 percent at 1.09 million, the group said in a statement.
Imported cars' market share increased to 70.4 percent in July from 64.4 percent a year earlier.

"The market was down for July, probably the result of more customers than usual holding off for August delivery and the new year identifier," said Roger King, SMMT Director of Public Affairs, in a statement.
"The first few days of August appear to confirm this."
General Motors Corp's Vauxhall unit led the market, accounting for 12.61 percent of cars registered in July compared to 13.39 percent in the year-ago month.

Ford Motor Co ranked second with 11.97 percent versus 14.56 percent, and Rover Group came in third, with 11.40 percent of the market compared to 14.18 percent. Rover is part of Germany's Bayerische Motoren-Werke AG.
